name: 049_tv_liquidity_sweep
hypothesis: TradingView port T6 (PLAN.md section 13) from the Pine v6 source the owner supplied: 'Liquidity Sweep Reversal Strategy' (Mozilla Public License 2.0). The author's claim: resting stops sit just beyond obvious swing highs/lows; a bar that runs those stops on a volume spike and then closes back inside with a long rejection wick has absorbed the stop-driven flow, so price reverts - long after a swept low, short after a swept high, once the next bar confirms past the sweep bar's midpoint, only in the 12:00-16:00 London/NY overlap. Counterparty: breakout traders and stopped-out traders forced to trade at the extreme. Author defaults kept: pivots 7/7, level max age 150 bars, min level spacing 0.25 ATR, volume > 1.3 x SMA20, wick:body >= 1.5, next-bar confirmation, session 1200-1600 exchange time (UTC on Binance) = UTC hours 12-15 of the signal bar, stop 1.2 ATR beyond the sweep wick, take-profit 1.5 R, break-even at 50% of the way to the target (= 0.75 R), longs and shorts. The script names no timeframe; 15m is used as the source (an intraday session strategy) and chart mode covers all seven. DEVIATIONS: (1) the stop is the engine's swing stop, n 2 (the sweep bar and the confirmation bar), 1.2 ATR buffer, measured from the fill (next open) instead of the confirmation close: it equals the script's stop unless the confirmation bar trades below the sweep wick, when it is wider; the script's 'reject if the stop < 0.5 ATR' can never fire with a 1.2 ATR buffer, so it is only kept as the clamp floor; (2) break-even: the script moves the stop when the intrabar high/low touches 0.75 R, the engine when a bar CLOSES past 0.75 R (checked on the previous close), so it moves later and less often; (3) the script freezes a pending sweep while a position is open and can act on it after the exit; the port cannot see the position, so a sweep that happens during a trade is dropped; (4) there is no time exit in the script; the engine needs one, it is a long safety cap and the only grid key; (5) costs: TradingView 0.04% commission and 1 tick slippage, here 0.05% taker + 0.02% slippage + funding; sizing 1% risk instead of 10% of equity; (6) pivot ties give no pivot (TradingView's tie rule is undocumented), ATR is Wilder-smoothed from the first bar rather than SMA-seeded (differs only in the first ~100 bars).
